summary: Documented M3-S03 (Email-to-Case routing addresses for support@/billing@, Web-to-Case intake, Case settings — Settings:Case, rebuilt once for F-25/F-26/F-27) after step-tester marked it tested. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md. Wrote three Section 6 workbook rows (CWB-AUT-007 the Settings:Case component, CWB-AUT-008 email-to-case-routing-addresses.md, CWB-AUT-009 web-to-case-form-contract.md, in workbook/06-automation.md) and two Other Configuration rows (CWB-OTHER-021 package.xml, CWB-OTHER-022 deploy-order.md); minted two new requirement ids (REQ-034 the two Email-to-Case routing addresses, REQ-035 Web-to-Case intake), continuing from the highest existing (REQ-033), and wrote their traceability.md Matrix rows plus a requirement-id-derivation pair. Appended two decisions (D-M3S03-01 — F-25's systemUserEmail is an attribution field, not a sender, so D-M3S02-04 stays open; D-M3S03-02 — F-27's forced casePriority is a new M3-gate decision affecting M4-S03, not pre-empted here even though the dry-run operator already amended M4-S03's own notes) and two open items (O-M3S03-01 — F-26's API >= 64.0 floor now leaves this build's package.xml files at two different versions with no plan-level field recording either, flagged as a build-planner v6 backlog item; O-M3S03-02 — the tester's own manual-test wording contradicts itself, 'exactly its three documented children' against a deliberate two-of-three omission the same sentence names, corrected as a record rather than by hand-editing acceptance_tests[].description). Cross-referenced REQ-005 (M1-S01's CaseOrigin row, which named M3 as its downstream consumer) and REQ-021 (M2-S04's fall-through-queue row, whose defaultCaseOwner is the field this step actually wires) in prose rather than duplicating either row — check_rtm.py enforces req_id uniqueness across the matrix, so a requirement already owning a row is cited, not re-rowed. Did not stage session-scratchpad UAT cases or Given/When/Then criteria for the two deferred manual tests this run, unlike the M3-S01/M3-S02 doc-keeper passes; both manual tests are recorded in traceability.md with their verbatim text and left for the M3-gate/compile-run UAT pack instead (extensions.uat_cases_staged is empty; see Process Observations, ambiguous). Set the step's status to documented via build_plan.py, then re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md again and ran check_rtm.py, which reported 0 coverage gaps, 0 orphans, 0 errors and 0 warnings across all 35 matrix rows. No other M3 step was running concurrently with this pass.
confidence_rationale: Every one of the step's four declared outputs plus the one undeclared deploy-order.md produced a workbook row (five rows total), both new traceability rows carry a real source_req_id freshly minted from requirement.md (L6-L8) and an answered clarification (Q17 for REQ-034, Q66 for REQ-035), and both rows name a verification cell stating what passed and what remains outstanding. check_rtm.py ran clean (0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 orphans) over the whole matrix, not just the two new rows. Re-running this pass would replace the same five workbook rows and two traceability rows rather than duplicate them (all keyed). Not MEDIUM: the step's type (`routing`) is a named row in Step 4's map (not a fallthrough to Other Configuration for the component itself — only package.xml/deploy-order.md use that default, consistent with every prior step), no artefact needed judgment to place in a section, and neither requirement id was inferred from an ambiguous field — both read directly off requirement.md's own intake-channel lines (L6-L8) plus one directly-answered clarification each. The decision not to stage scratchpad UAT cases this run is a scope choice, not a gap: agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 7 does not require it, and the final UAT pack is Step 10's job at the milestone compile step, which has not run.

process_observations.observation: check_rtm.py's req_id-uniqueness rule (an ERROR, not a WARN) was checked before writing any new row, which is why REQ-005 and REQ-021 were cross-referenced in prose rather than given a second row each for M3-S03 — the matrix stayed at exactly 35 rows with 0 duplicate-req_id errors on the actual lint run, not merely by intent.

The rebuild's three field-level changes (F-25/F-26/F-27) and the one manifest-version change were verified against the actual on-disk artefact (settings/Case.settings-meta.xml, package.xml) rather than only against the builder's own prose, before being written into the workbook and traceability rows.

F-27's forced casePriority default permanently disables M4-S03's null-guarded Priority stamp for email-originated Cases, and that consequence is only partly recorded in the plan today: the dry-run operator amended M4-S03's own notes, but the actual three-way choice (accept Medium / derive-and-overwrite / other) is still unmade, and nothing currently blocks M4-S03 from being built against the stale plan wording before the M3 gate resolves it.

This build now carries two package.xml API versions (67.0 on M3-S03, 62.0 on every M1/M2 step) with no plan-level field recording either as the build's version — mock_deploy.py's own tooling fix (computing the highest version across the steps selected in one request) is what let Run 5 validate the mixed set, not anything in plan.json itself.

plan.json steps[M3-S03].acceptance_tests[3].description asserts the webToCase block carries 'exactly its three documented children' while, in the same sentence, naming the deliberate omission of the third — the two clauses cannot both be true, and the artefact matches the omission, not the count. Recorded as O-M3S03-02 rather than hand-edited, since this agent does not touch acceptance_tests[].description.

No session-scratchpad UAT case or Given/When/Then criterion was staged for TC-M3S03-01/TC-M3S03-02 this run, unlike the M3-S01/M3-S02 precedent of compiling a manual test into a linted case pre-emptively. Both test ids appear in traceability.md as manual, deferred tests with their verbatim acceptance-test text; whether the M3 gate expects them pre-compiled or expects the milestone-compile step (Step 10, not yet run) to produce them first is not stated anywhere this agent can read.

M3-S03 is documented; M3-S04 is the next pending M3 step and the one that both exercises decisions.md D-M3S02-04 (senderEmail) and must read D-M3S03-02 before its own Priority-stamping logic (in M4-S03) is finalized.
